identificationModule.briefTitle: Creatine and Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate (HMB) Supplementation Plus Home-Based Exercise for Sarcopenia in Huntington's Disease
identificationModule.officialTitle: Multi-Omic Biomarkers of Response to an Integrated Intervention (Home-Based Multicomponent Exercise Plus Creatine and/or Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate [HMB] Supplementation) to Reduce Sarcopenia and Preserve Muscle and Functional Capacity in Huntington's Disease: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Four-Arm Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Huntington's disease (HD) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder in which accelerated loss of muscle mass, strength and autonomy (physical frailty and sarcopenia) contributes to functional decline. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, four-arm parallel trial will include adults with HD and physical frailty/sarcopenia. All participants will follow a 12-week individualized, home-based multicomponent exercise program (VIVIFRAIL-based, with weekly remote monitoring) and will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo, creatine (CRE), beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) or combined CRE+HMB. The study will test whether combined CRE+HMB produces synergistic improvements in functional capacity, neuromuscular performance, body composition, cognition and quality of life, and will use multi-omic profiling (circulating and extracellular-vesicle microRNAs, plasma proteomics and genetics) to identify mechanisms and predictive signatures of response. Durability of effects will be assessed 6 months after the end of the intervention.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, four-arm parallel-group trial conducted at the Neurology Department of Hospital Universitario de Burgos (HUBU; recruitment, clinical assessment, biological sampling) and the University of Burgos (UBU; exercise physiology, functional testing and multi-omic analyses).

Randomization: computer-generated permuted blocks of variable size (REDCap), 1:1:1:1 allocation, stratified by sex, antipsychotic use, participation in structured exercise programs and diabetes. Allocation is performed and concealed by an independent pharmacist (HUBU Pharmacy Service). Participants, intervention staff, outcome assessors and data analysts are blinded; supplements are packed in identical coded sachets.

Interventions: once daily for 12 weeks, dissolved in 100 mL fruit juice with the evening meal: (1) 3 g creatine monohydrate + 3 g microcrystalline cellulose; (2) 3 g beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) + 3 g cellulose; (3) 3 g creatine + 3 g HMB; (4) placebo, 6 g microcrystalline cellulose. All participants follow a Mediterranean-style diet (protein 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day) and an individualized home-based multicomponent exercise program based on VIVIFRAIL, prescribed and supervised by an occupational therapist, with weekly phone calls to monitor adherence, perceived exertion (target Borg rating of perceived exertion \[RPE\] 12-15) and adverse events. Adherence is monitored by intake logs and sachet counts.

Assessments: baseline (T0), week 12 (T1, end of intervention) and 6-month follow-up (T2). Functional capacity (Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale \[UHDRS\] Total Functional Capacity \[TFC\], Functional Assessment Scale, Independence Scale, gait speed, Short Physical Performance Battery \[SPPB\]), body composition (multifrequency bioimpedance), neuromuscular function (rate of force development and peak force during isometric knee extension), cognition (Mini-Mental State Examination \[MMSE\], Symbol Digit Modalities Test \[SDMT\], Stroop test, Trail Making Test \[TMT\], verbal fluency), quality of life (12-Item Short Form Health Survey \[SF-12\]) and adverse events. Fasting blood samples for small RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of circulating and extracellular-vesicle microRNAs (with quantitative polymerase chain reaction \[qPCR\] validation), plasma proteomics (Olink Reveal, 1,034 proteins) and pharmacogenetics (15 single nucleotide polymorphisms \[SNPs\] in SLC6A8, CKM, GATM, MTOR, AKT1, PTEN; genome-wide genotyping in a subset).

Sample size: 64 participants (16 per arm) are needed to detect a small-to-moderate effect (f = 0.20) on change in TFC (alpha 0.05, power 0.80, r = 0.50); allowing for 25-30% dropout, 84-88 participants will be enrolled.

Statistical analysis: intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses; linear mixed-effects models with Group x Time interaction and pre-specified contrasts of creatine (CRE)+HMB versus each single supplement and placebo; multi-omic integration (mixOmics/DIABLO, MOFA+, elastic net, random forest) with repeated nested cross-validation to identify predictive signatures of response.

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: Four-arm parallel-group trial (placebo, creatine, beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate \[HMB\], creatine+HMB); all arms also receive the same individualized home-based multicomponent exercise program. eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older with genetically confirmed Huntington's disease (HD) (cytosine-adenine-guanine \[CAG\] repeat expansion in the huntingtin \[HTT\] gene).
* Symptomatic HD, defined by a Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) total motor score \> 4, in early-intermediate stages according to Total Functional Capacity (TFC).
* Physical frailty and/or sarcopenia, defined as Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score \<= 10 and/or gait speed \< 1.0 m/s and/or European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) sarcopenia criteria (low strength and low muscle quantity/quality assessed by validated bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-derived indices).
* VIVIFRAIL category B (frail) or C1/C2 (pre-frail).
* Stable pharmacological treatment for at least 4 weeks before baseline.
* Clinical judgement of the neurologist and occupational therapist that the participant can safely perform a prescribed home-based exercise program with weekly remote monitoring.
* Written informed consent from the participant or legally authorized representative (with participant assent whenever possible).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unstable cardiovascular, renal, hepatic or musculoskeletal disease contraindicating exercise or supplementation.
* Severe chorea or postural instability preventing safe training; uncontrolled psychiatric symptoms or active substance abuse.
* Severe dysphagia preventing safe intake of thickened liquids (unless a clinically acceptable alternative exists).
* Allergy or intolerance to any supplement component.
* Pregnancy or lactation.
* Use of protein supplements in the month before inclusion.

identificationModule.briefTitle: Creatine and Muscle Health in Madrid's Walking Footballers.
identificationModule.officialTitle: Effects of Creatine Supplementation on Muscle Health in Madrid's Older Walking Footballers

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Healthy aging requires effective, accessible, and sustainable interventions capable of preserving functional capacity and preventing age-related decline. In this context, walking football has emerged as a safe, inclusive physical exercise modality with high adherence among older adults, demonstrating benefits for muscle health, metabolic profile, and psychosocial well-being. On the other hand, creatine monohydrate supplementation is backed by robust scientific evidence as a strategy to enhance exercise adaptations, promote muscle mass maintenance, and improve factors related to metabolic syndrome.

The objective of this project is to evaluate the effects of creatine supplementation combined with regular walking football practice on muscle quality and metabolic profile in older adults, as well as to explore the underlying biological mechanisms using a cell culture-based experimental model. The ultimate goal is to determine the potential of this intervention to promote healthy longevity through functional, muscular, and metabolic indicators associated with healthspan.

Specifically, the study will analyze the intervention's effects on body composition, physical fitness, and metabolic syndrome markers; evaluate its impact on psychosocial well-being, quality of life, and cognitive function; and investigate the molecular mechanisms related to muscle health, protection against oxidative stress, and the modulation of senescence using an ex vivo/in vitro model.

The project will be carried out in two complementary phases. First, a longitudinal experimental study will be conducted in older adults participating in walking football programs and supplemented with creatine. Subsequently, skeletal muscle cultures will be exposed to conditioned sera obtained before and after the intervention to investigate its biological effects.

This approach will integrate the evaluation of clinical efficacy with the study of the underlying mechanisms, generating applicable knowledge for designing personalized, sustainable, and cost-effective strategies to prevent sarcopenia and metabolic syndrome.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Individuals over 50 years of age
* Minimum physical activity level recommended by the World Health Organization (≥150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity or ≥75 minutes of vigorous-intensity activity per week)
* Men and women with regular participation (≥2 times per week) in walking football training for at least 6 months
* Voluntary acceptance to participate in the study after having read, understood, and signed the informed consent form.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of metabolic, neuromuscular, cardiovascular, or joint diseases that contraindicate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and/or creatine supplementation
* Current use of creatine nutritional supplements or other ergogenic compounds
* Having any comprehension difficulties or presenting musculoskeletal alterations that influence the assessments
* Being under pharmacological treatment that may alter muscle mass or function
* Cognitive impairment or alteration that prevents following the protocol indications.
